settings.bio: Joidart is a Barcelona-based jewellery company started in 1981 by Jaume Julià.  Julià turned a small gold and silversmith's workshop near the Costa Brava into a contemporary jewellery house with art at its centre. Working with designers from Barcelona's Escola Massana, the brand built a language of aesthetic purity,  with collections that interpret Joan Miró and Antoni Gaudí. Now led by Jaume's daughters, Cristina and Mariona, Joidart still makes its pieces slowly and in short runs from its own workshop, a family house carrying its founder's spirit forward.

settings.location: West Yorkshire · Contemporary Jewellery & Object Design
settings.bio: Will Sharp is a contemporary jeweller whose work combines geometry, modular form, and sustainable design through a distinctly modernist lens. A first-class graduate of The Glasgow School of Art, he works with recycled silver, digital fabrication, and PLA - a renewable plant-based bioplastic rarely used in contemporary jewellery. In 2019 he received both the Hallmark Studio New Designers Award and the Association of Contemporary Jewellers Mark Fenn Award. His work has been stocked and commissioned by institutions including the Tate, The Hepworth Wakefield, Baltic Centre for Contemporary Art, and the London Museum.

Founded in Edinburgh in 2020, Janus takes its name from the Roman god of beginnings, endings and transitions. After more than a decade in the UK industry as a jewellery buyer and retailer, Di set out to make her own in premium sterling silver and gold that hold a quiet vintage feeling within a modern line.

Kirsty Thomas is the artist and founder behind Tom Pigeon, a design studio creating jewellery in small batches. Inspired by modern art and architectural colour blocking, the designs balance bold colour with simple shapes, and each one functions as a small piece of wearable sculpture. Kirsty pays careful attention to colour and form; her work has been made for The Barbican, the V&A, Tate Modern and The Design Museum, alongside Atelier Modernista.

Claire is a Welsh jewellery designer whose work combines sculptural form, expressive colour, and contemporary craftsmanship, often inspired by symbolism, language, and modern art. Designed using recycled precious metals and responsibly sourced materials, her pieces have been featured in Elle, Tatler, Stylist, Grazia, and The Guardian, and she was named Boutique Magazine’s Best Accessories Brand in 2023.

Justine Nettleton creates enamel jewellery as 830 Degrees from her Nottingham studio. With a background in Fine Art, her small-batch pieces celebrate material transformation and expressive surface design. Using kiln-fired enamel fused onto copper, she builds colour and texture - each firing producing subtle variations in tone and surface, making every piece unique.

Mia Houghton is the founder of Mijoux Creations, working in silver using traditional bench techniques alongside enamel. Inspired by nature, she previously worked for Boodles and De Beers in London before setting up her Salisbury-based studio practice, where she focuses on small-batch jewellery. Her work reflects an interest in colour, movement and geometry; traditional bench techniques and careful finishing give her pieces a delicate presence.

Claire founded Copper Bee in 2019, working from her Wiltshire studio. Working primarily with copper and mixed metals, she uses traditional forming and texturing techniques to create warm, tactile surfaces. Her small-batch pieces celebrate colour, individuality, and the character of hand-worked materials.

Jenni Douglas is a Scottish designer-maker known for joyful geometric compositions inspired by Mid-Century Modern design, architecture, and everyday colour. Beginning with original linocuts and illustrations, her work expands into jewellery, textiles, and homeware designed and produced in Scotland. Her pieces are stocked by organisations including The Scottish Parliament and The Scottish Design Exchange, and are recognised for their playful modernism and strong graphic identity.

settings.location: Buenos Aires · Sculptural leather & mixed materials
settings.bio: Iskin Sisters is the design house of Gabriela and Karina Iskin, half-Brazilian, half-Argentinian sisters working from Buenos Aires since 2004. Their pieces take an architectural approach to unconventional materials — leather, acrylic, stainless steel — each one built as a small, conceptual study in form. Drawn from childhood, nature and travel, the collections read as wearable geometry: bold, sculptural, and slightly apart from anything else on the wall. Their work has been selected for museum stores worldwide and shown at Maison&Objet in Paris.

settings.location: London · Geometric jewellery in laminate & silver
settings.bio: Emily Kidson trained in Three Dimensional Crafts at the University of Brighton, then spent a year at the Bishopsland Educational Trust refining her metalwork. Her pieces layer silver, gold, wood and richly coloured Formica laminate into compositions built on repetition, pattern and precise negative space — a language borrowed from old industrial buildings, chimneys and canal-side architecture. Since returning to the bench after a decade as an art librarian, she has shown at COLLECT at the Saatchi Gallery and the Goldsmiths' Fair, and won the Design Trust Award at Made London.

settings.location: London · Fine and fashion jewellery, sculptural and edge-driven
settings.bio: Kasun London is the label of Kasun Ekanayake, a Sri Lankan-born, New Zealand-raised designer who trained in industrial design before learning jewellery-making under goldsmith Graham Shirley. He built the brand in London from 2011, working across a range that stretches from soft, birthstone pieces to gothic-edged motifs — skulls, claws, fangs. His work has been worn by Kendall Jenner, Halsey and Jenna Ortega, and the studio holds multiple Goldsmiths' Craft & Design Council awards.

Beira is the studio practice of Irene Reyes, working in kiln-formed glass from the south of Spain. Reyes treats colour as the starting point of every piece — the material's memory and mood — building forms through repeated cycles of heat, controlled cooling, and hand-finished cutting and polishing. Made in small, limited series, the results sit somewhere between object and jewellery: abstracted, minimal, and drawn from the landscape around her studio.

settings.heading: Artists & Designers
settings.intro: Atelier Modernista is a curated gallery for unusual contemporary jewellery. These are the independent artists and designers whose work, innovation, sustainability, and imagination we love and have chosen to bring together here at Atelier Modernista.
